title: Reliability arithmetic
point: End-to-end success is per-step success raised to the number of steps, so long chains fail far more often than any single step suggests.
definition: If each step succeeds independently with probability p, a run of n steps succeeds with probability p to the power n. The maximum number of steps for a target T is floor(ln T / ln p).

objective.text: Compute end-to-end success for a given chain and the maximum step count for a target, then choose between fewer steps, verification and checkpoints to close the gap.

misconceptions.claim: A 95 per cent reliable step makes a 95 per cent reliable agent.
misconceptions.correction: Success compounds. Twenty steps at 0.95 give about 0.36 end to end, so the agent fails nearly two runs in three.

misconceptions.claim: Retries make every step effectively perfect.
misconceptions.correction: Retries only help with faults that a check can detect. A confidently wrong step passes straight through unless something verifies its output.

l1: Success compounds multiplicatively. 0.98^10 is about 0.82, 0.95^20 is about 0.36, and 0.99^50 is about 0.61.
To find the most steps you can afford for a target T at per-step success p, compute floor(ln T / ln p).
There are three levers: use fewer steps, raise per-step reliability through verification or retries, or add checkpoints so a failed step can be recovered instead of restarting the run.
l2: A team needs 0.90 end to end, and each step succeeds 0.98 of the time. ln 0.90 divided by ln 0.98 is about 5.2, so the limit is 5 steps.
Their plan has 12 steps, which gives 0.98^12, about 0.78. That misses the target by a wide margin.
Adding verification that lifts each step to 0.995 gives 0.995^12, about 0.94. The plan keeps its 12 steps and clears the target.
l3: Checkpoints are the third lever. Split the 12 steps into three stages of four; each stage succeeds with 0.98^4, about 0.92, and a failed stage reruns from its checkpoint.
Allowing one rerun per stage lifts each stage to about 0.994, and the three-stage run to about 0.98. This assumes failures are detected at the stage boundary and are independent.
The price is up to about 8 per cent more steps on average, plus checkpoint storage. State that cost next to the gain when you defend the design.
